clue.text: Foreign article covering a sport

indicators.note: to cover is to go over and around, so the article wraps itself round the next piece; the same word also supplies that piece

blocks.note: the French masculine definite article
covering a distance is going across it

explanation.surface: A newspaper's foreign article reports on some sporting event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' does double duty: it supplies the inner word (covering ground is going across it) and tells you the article wraps around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a team game played with netted sticks, originally from North America, so it is one example of a sport.

clue.text: New cast learn of predecessors

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so the following letters are put into a fresh order

blocks.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A fresh set of actors finds out about the ones who played the roles before them.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancestral describes things coming from forebears, so 'of predecessors' is a phrase meaning the same adjective.

clue.text: Compass displaying north in storm

indicators.note: one letter sits inside the word for the storm

blocks.note: to storm is to rage
the map abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A navigator's compass shows which way is north in the middle of a gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compass' looks like the instrument, tying in with north, but it means scope or extent.
explanation.definitionFit: Compass in the sense of scope or reach is a synonym of range, as in the range of someone's knowledge.

clue.text: You could say one’s a non-chain rental service

definitions.note: names a business; the answer is a phrase for a small landlord

blocks.note: first meaning: the letter i, which stands for one, is a lower-case character
second meaning: an independent landlord letting property on a modest scale, not a big agency chain

explanation.surface: Someone describes themselves as an independent lettings agent rather than part of a big chain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You could say' flags the first meaning as a playful one: the numeral one written as a letter i. A letter is also one who lets property.
explanation.definitionFit: Lower-case type is printed in small letters, and a letter of houses is a landlord, so a small one is an independent landlord.

clue.text: Pull out old treatise

blocks.note: ex- means former, as in an ex-wife
a tract is a short written treatise

explanation.surface: Someone retrieves an ancient learned essay from the archive.
explanation.definitionFit: To extract something is to draw or remove it, so it is a verb synonym of pull out.

clue.text: One longing to get rid of York’s premier brass maker

indicators.note: getting rid of something removes it, here the first letter named next

blocks.note: one who yearns, or longs
the first letter of York

explanation.surface: Someone eager to leave York sets up as a metalworker making brass goods.
explanation.walkthrough: Brass is British slang for money, so a brass maker is someone who makes money.
explanation.definitionFit: An earner brings in income, and brass is slang for money, so the earner is one who makes money.

clue.text: Sport that doesn’t hold wife’s attention

indicators.note: not holding something means it is left out of the word

blocks.note: to sport clothes is to wear them
the standard abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A game that fails to keep a spouse interested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sport' looks like a game, but here it is the verb meaning to wear something showily.
explanation.definitionFit: To have someone's ear means to have their attention, a common idiom in which the noun stands for listening.

clue.text: Isn’t a rest fantastic for irritability

indicators.note: fantastic means fanciful or far-fetched, so the letters are reshaped freely

blocks.note: the nine letters to rearrange, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question: wouldn't a lovely break cure a bad temper?
explanation.definitionFit: Ratty is British slang for bad-tempered, so rattiness is crotchety irritability, the noun for being tetchy.

clue.text: English policeman upset, getting hard time

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns a word upside down so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: the abbreviation for English
informal word for a police officer
H for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A distressed English constable is given a tough period, perhaps in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: E, then the policeman flipped, then H.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is an era or long period of history, so it is a specific kind of time.

clue.text: One charged to protect conservative figure

indicators.note: protecting something means surrounding it, so the next letter goes inside

blocks.note: an ion is an atom carrying an electric charge
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A man accused of a crime is shielding a right-wing personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One charged' reads as an accused person; it is the chemist's charged particle.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is an image or emblematic representation, so it is a figure in the sense of a picture or symbol.

clue.text: Change weekly alcohol units, perhaps, over time

indicators.note: the beer word is laid over and around the time letter, enclosing it

blocks.note: a weekly allowance of beer could be called an ale ration
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone revises the number of drinks they allow themselves each week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks ale ration as one example of a weekly quota of alcohol units; T goes after AL.
explanation.definitionFit: An alteration is a modification, so it is a noun synonym of change.

clue.text: Too fab, essentially wonderful

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only its middle letter is used

blocks.note: the centre letter of fab
swell is old-fashioned slang for excellent

explanation.surface: Something is excessively great, really marvellous at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Too fab' reads as gushing praise, but 'Too' is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: As well and too both mean in addition or also, so the phrase swaps for the adverb directly.

clue.text: Burning houses labourer evacuated unhurt

indicators.note: a building houses its occupants, so the burning word holds the next letters inside it
an evacuated building is emptied, so the word loses everything between its ends

blocks.note: alight means on fire
the first and last letters of labourer

explanation.surface: A worker escapes a blazing building without injury.
explanation.walkthrough: AL, then LR, then IGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: If someone is all right after an accident they are safe and uninjured, the same as being unhurt.

clue.text: Chap who makes kids properly cross before school?

definitions.text: Chap who makes kids properly cross before school?

blocks.clueFragment: Chap who makes kids properly cross
blocks.note: surface reading: a man who annoys children thoroughly
setter's reading: he helps children walk safely across the road on their way to lessons

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a lollipop man is a school crossing patrol officer, named for his round stop sign on a pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A school crossing patrol stops traffic so pupils can get over the road safely, which is making them cross properly.

clue.text: Cosmetic surgery’s needed for lean matron

indicators.note: surgery reshapes a body, so the letters that follow are reconstructed

blocks.note: the ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A thin hospital matron wants a nip and tuck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cosmetic surgery' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops after the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ornamental is decorative rather than functional, which is one sense of cosmetic, meaning only for show.

clue.text: Great deal for a roll plus salsa?

blocks.note: taken as written
a bread roll, or a bun
salsa is one kind of dance, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A shopper spots a bargain on bread rolls and a tomato dip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roll plus salsa' suggests food, but salsa is the Latin dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundance is a plentiful supply, a large quantity, which is what 'a great deal' means as a noun phrase.

clue.text: Christ appearing in England, oddly

indicators.note: oddly points to the letters in odd-numbered positions only

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of England

explanation.surface: A report of the Second Coming happening in England, which would be strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Christ' is not the person but the exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Egad is an old-fashioned exclamation of surprise, like the oath someone shouts when startled.

clue.text: Love is not a road I travelled

indicators.note: letters that have travelled have moved about from their original places

blocks.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A wistful line: romance is a path I never took.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is deep devoted affection or worship, so it is a noun for intense love.

clue.text: Some overclouding point of great interest

indicators.note: only some of the next word is taken, a run of its letters

blocks.note: letters three to six of overclouding

explanation.surface: Clouds gathering over something are the most dramatic part of the view.
explanation.walkthrough: CLOU is a word borrowed from French, literally nail, for the main attraction or high point.
explanation.definitionFit: The clou of a show or event is its chief attraction, the centre of attention, a rare borrowing used in English.

clue.text: John McEnroe often put his foot in it

definitions.text: John McEnroe often put his foot in it

blocks.note: surface reading: the famously hot-headed player often said something tactless

blocks.clueFragment: John McEnroe often put his foot in it
blocks.note: setter's reading: the player literally put his foot inside a piece of footwear made for his sport

explanation.walkthrough: John McEnroe is an American tennis champion known for his outbursts at umpires, which makes the idiom fit.
explanation.definitionFit: A court player wears a soft rubber-soled shoe made for the game, so his foot went into one every match.

clue.text: Starting out on climb, nervous initially

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word before it

blocks.note: the first letter of nervous
an ascent is a climb

explanation.surface: A climber setting off up a mountain feels a little anxious at first.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' puts the letter on top of the climb word.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent means just coming into being, beginning to develop, which is what starting out means as an adjective.

clue.text: Land our hands cultivated

indicators.note: cultivated soil is turned over and worked, so the letters are turned into a new order

blocks.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A field that we farmed with our own hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land' looks like soil to be farmed, but it is a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Honduras is a Central American country, so it is one example of a land or nation.

clue.text: Talk over singer, that’s rude ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word before it

blocks.note: O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over
a singer is underworld slang for an informer, as is a rat
the last letter of rude

explanation.surface: Chatting over the top of a vocalist is bad manners in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: A singer here is someone who sings to the police, an informer; O stands for over in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to give a speech, often pompously, so it is a verb for talking at length.

clue.text: Boyfriend chasing former PA?

blocks.note: old as in one's old school, meaning former
a woman's man is her boyfriend

explanation.surface: A man pursues the woman who used to be his personal assistant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chasing' puts the boyfriend after the word for former. PA reads as personal assistant, but it is dad; the question mark flags this.
explanation.definitionFit: Old man is informal slang for one's father, the same as pa, a casual word for dad.

clue.text: Fancy shot taken round central Leeds

indicators.note: central points to the single middle letter of the place name
something taken round another goes around it, enclosing it

blocks.note: a dram is a shot of whisky
the third of the five letters of Leeds

explanation.surface: A clever photograph taken in the middle of Leeds, a northern English city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' suggests a photograph but is a measure of spirits; DR, then E, then AM.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy something is to imagine it, and to dream is also to picture or imagine, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Sea mist over Ramsgate front is normal

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter
the mist lies over the letter, covering it on both sides

blocks.note: the main is a poetic word for the open sea
steam is a kind of mist or vapour
the first letter of Ramsgate

explanation.surface: Fog rolling in off the water at Ramsgate, a seaside town in Kent, is quite usual.
explanation.walkthrough: MAIN, then ST, R, EAM: the mist word surrounds R.
explanation.definitionFit: Mainstream describes what is conventional or widely accepted, which is an adjective sense of normal.

clue.text: Rubbish piece of needlework?

blocks.note: first meaning: cheap tasteless goods, junk
second meaning: to make tatting, a knotted lace

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a bit of embroidery as worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the stretch: tat is a verb for making lace, not strictly a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Tat is British slang for tawdry junk, and tatting is handmade lace knotted with a shuttle.

clue.text: Send back American periodical

indicators.note: sending back means the magazine's name is read the other way

blocks.note: Time is a US weekly news magazine

explanation.surface: Someone returns a US magazine to the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Send back' reads as one verb, but 'back' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to send out or give off, as a radio emits a signal, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Feel aggrieved at being powerless here

indicators.note: being without power means the symbol for it is taken out of the word

blocks.note: being here means being present
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Someone is bitter at having no influence in this place.
explanation.definitionFit: To resent something is to feel bitterness or indignation about it, so it is a verb for feeling aggrieved.

clue.text: Building alteration? Concrete’s first to go

indicators.note: the opening letter is made to go, dropping it from the word

blocks.note: this puzzle's entry 10-across is the word alteration
cement is the binder in concrete, used loosely for it

explanation.surface: A building is altered and the concrete is the first thing ripped out.
explanation.walkthrough: A cross-reference: ALTERATION is the answer at 10, so 'alteration?' gives the number TEN. CEMENT then loses its C.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenement is a large building divided into flats, so it is one kind of building, common in Scottish cities.
